reference_logic.mechanism: 把解释的可信度分解为三层并分别约束：第一层是依据可追溯，即对文献按段落与证据边界建索引，对运行参数按版本建独立知识，使每条解释都附带来源，从而压低无依据陈述；第二层是动作忠实，即文献检索只能保证“有出处”，不能保证解释与当前动作的实际电气效应一致，因此对关键动作构造可行的反事实（在保持功率平衡与设备边界的前提下替换或撤销动作，再重算交流潮流并比较关键支路），把解释中的方向描述与仿真里的动作效应绑定；第三层是人员效益，即解释是否真正帮助识别错误方案与缩短复核。中介路径为：有效证据覆盖与不适用规则过滤→解释方向与仿真一致→错误方案识别与复核效率。该机制的作用范围限于仿真内的动作效应检验，并明确不声称识别现实因果或提供安全保证；证据不足时输出“无法支持”，缺平衡资源的反事实判为不可检验。
reference_logic.evidence_needs: 需要四类可核查材料：(1) 带可追溯段落与合法访问来源的文献索引，用于支撑灵敏度方向、约束校验与交直流动作重算等具体断言；(2) 版本化的运行知识与拓扑配置，用以标记过期规则并支持知识版本过滤；(3) 固定候选方案集，须覆盖正确方案、方向错误、潜在新过载、过期拓扑规则和不可检验反事实五类，并配套统一潮流仿真与可用的平衡资源；(4) 双人独立标注及其一致性统计，以及人工复核时间与随机交叉顺序的实验记录。需要强调的是，文献只能支撑底层电气关系与约束校验，检索忠实性、反事实解释的增量作用和人工复核收益属于待检验命题，不能当作既有证据引用；引用支持率、方向一致率等指标本身也需在标注协议中先定义。
reference_logic.verification: 采用分层对照：至少200个固定候选方案的盲测集，按文档与拓扑分组留出以避免泄漏；对比无检索、仅检索、检索加反事实三组，并增设纯数值校核作为额外基线，以区分“解释起了作用”与“安全校核直接给出答案”。指标分别报告引用支持率、解释与仿真方向一致率、错误方案识别的精确率与召回率（在等误报率下比较召回）、解释延迟与人工复核时间。阴性判据预先设定：若引用支持率上升但忠实性无改善，或解释仅复述安全校核结论，则不成立反事实解释的增量贡献。人工部分采用随机交叉顺序控制学习效应，报告标注者间一致性，并在未完成人工实验时仅声明自动指标结论。
reference_logic.gaps: (1) 反事实依赖可行替代平衡资源，缺失时判为不可检验，导致可检验样本比例下降并可能引入选择性偏差；(2) 文献仅6篇，过期规则与拓扑不一致情形的覆盖偏窄，过滤率的估计不稳定；(3) 方向一致率是忠实性的代理指标，其构念效度未单独论证，且引用支持率与忠实性若由同一标注者判定存在混淆风险，需盲法与分人标注；(4) 固定动作集虽隔离了解释效应，但限制了对其他调控场景的外推；(5) 解释异步生成与独立安全校核并行的时序影响（如解释滞后导致的决策等待）未被量化为独立变量；(6) 未进入闭环下发，仅离线评估，生态效度与真实调度压力下的表现未知；(7) 人工复核收益受审核者背景影响，样本量与个体差异需要更大规模实验才能区分组间差异与噪声。

context.core_mechanism_constraint: 假设文献检索减少无依据陈述，但仅检索不能保证解释忠实于当前动作；反事实潮流干预将说明与实际电气效应绑定，从而揭示错误方向、过期规则或遗漏受影响线路。该干预用于检验仿真内的动作作用，不宣称识别所有现实因果效应。

The results show that SAC reduces the daily operation cost to 45,820 USD, decreases the renewable curtailment rate to 4.82%, and lowers load shedding to 0.71 MWh under 70% wind-solar penetration. hits.file: Interpretable Machine Learning Models for Critical Decision Systems
hits.text: ailable to humans. This paper is the systematic and complete study of interpretable machine learning models of critical decision systems. We start by examining the conceptual basis behind interpretability and its significance in high risk applications. An elaborate literature review classifies the currently existing interpretability methods as intrinsic interpretability methods and post-hoc explanation methods and their strong and weak points and the appropriateness to critical systems. The suggested methodology describes a systematic approach to the selection, design and validation of interpretable ML models within real-life conditions of uncertainties of data, bias and regulatory standards. Mathematically stated representative interpretable models such as linear models, decision trees, rule-based systems and attention mechanisms are given to provide formal grounding. Examples of experimental findings of representative domains of application are presented to illustrate the trade-offs in interpretability and performance. The discussion highlights levels of interpretability, robustness, and fairness measures, and predictive accuracy.

Temporary industrial load reduction releases capacity during outages but creates recovery obligations that compete with later load restoration and storage charging. We study a topology-aware restoration controller with staged correction of discrete network decisions and continuous industrial and storage actions, followed by bounded candidate screening. The modified IEEE 33-bus and 69-bus feeders are each evaluated over 440 matched physical scenarios and three independently trained policies, giving 3960 complete 96-step cases per feeder. Then, a screening method for major congestion scenario is proposed based on the shadow price theory. hits.file: Rule-Based Real-Time Energy Management System for Curative Congestion Management in Low-Voltage Distribution Grids
hits.text: The electrification of residential demand through electric vehicles (EVs), heat pumps (HPs), photovoltaic (PV) systems, and battery energy storage systems (BESSs) creates new congestion challenges in low-voltage (LV) grids. This study evaluates a transparent, deterministic, and real-time-capable rule-based energy management system (EMS) for curative thermal congestion management within a §14a EnWG-oriented setting. The EMS is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink and tested on a representative four-feeder LV network supplying 56 households. Congestion is detected from maximum phase root-mean-square currents using conservative transformer and feeder thresholds. After a threshold is reached, the EMS first activates available BESS support and then applies simultaneous feeder-wide EV limitation, batched round-robin curtailment, or staged feeder-wide reduction toward 4.2 kW. hits.file: Adversarial Self‐Improvement for Resilient Smart Grid Dispatch Control Under Extreme N‐2 Contingencies
hits.text: ABSTRACT Deploying AI‐enabled dispatch controllers in smart grids demands quantifiable resilience against contingencies beyond the conventional N‐1 design basis. We present AG2CDT + , an adversarial self‐improvement framework that hardens offline‐trained dispatch controllers through iterative stress testing and corrective fine‐tuning. A grid adversary generates targeted N‐1, N‐2 and compound contingencies from critical transmission corridors. A safety oracle combining PTDF‐based preaction thermal screening, an advisory AC Jacobian voltage‐sensitivity predictor and duration‐aware poststep voltage enforcement identifies violations and generates corrected actions via line search; a special protection scheme (SPS) controller invokes targeted load shedding and line‐bridge switching whenever AC power flow diverges turning previously‐fatal scenarios into recoverable ones. hits.file: Resilience‐based tri‐level framework for simultaneous transmission and substation expansion planning considering extreme weather‐related events
hits.text: In this study, a new resilience‐based framework is presented for multi‐period simultaneous transmission and substation expansion planning (ST&SEP) considering extreme weather‐related events (EWEs). The formation of the proposed planning framework falls into a tri‐level optimisation problem with the aim of strengthening power network resilience in response to the EWEs. In the lower‐level problem, short‐term remedial corrective strategies of the independent system operator (ISO) after the EWEs are determined by applying network reconfiguration and generation redispatch. In the intermediate‐level problem, an enhanced scenario‐building approach is developed to model and analyse the EWEs, as non‐random uncertain events, and their subsequent detrimental effects using the notion of the fragility curves corresponding to power network components. hits.file: A Distributed Optimization Algorithm for Multi-Area Power Grid Transmission Congestion Management
hits.text: Abstract The interconnection of power grid brings significant economic benefits, while it calls for higher requirements to the security, stability and economic operation of power system as well. With high dimensionality of its optimization problem, the whole network centralized optimal power flow (OPF) algorithm is computational inefficient. Therefore, on the basis of power grid layering and zoning, the distributed optimal power flow calculation method in interconnected power grid with multiple control centers has important realistic significance. A distributed optimization algorithm of interconnected power grid transmission congestion management is proposed in this paper. hits.file: Hierarchical AI Control and Protection for Renewable Multi-Terminal HVDC Grids
hits.text: General Background: The transition toward large-scale wind and solar integration requires transmission infrastructures capable of stable long-distance power delivery. Specific Background: Multi-terminal VSC-HVDC grids provide this capability but introduce complex coordination challenges in control and ultra-fast DC fault protection. Knowledge Gap: Existing studies treat advanced control and protection as separate problems, limiting system-level coordination during disturbances and contingencies. Aims: This study develops a unified hierarchical AI-driven architecture that integrates deep reinforcement learning (DRL) for primary converter control, an AI-based secondary coordinator for system-wide optimization, and a CNN-assisted hybrid protection scheme for rapid fault management. hits.file: TimeREISE: Time Series Randomized Evolving Input Sample Explanation
hits.text: Deep neural networks are one of the most successful classifiers across different domains. However, their use is limited in safety-critical areas due to their limitations concerning interpretability. The research field of explainable artificial intelligence addresses this problem. However, most interpretability methods align to the imaging modality by design. The paper introduces TimeREISE, a model agnostic attribution method that shows success in the context of time series classification. The method applies perturbations to the input and considers different attribution map characteristics such as the granularity and density of an attribution map. The approach demonstrates superior performance compared to existing methods concerning different well-established measurements. TimeREISE shows impressive results in the deletion and insertion test, Infidelity, and Sensitivity. hits.file: Topology-Aware Graph Reinforcement Learning for Voltage-Reactive Power Control in Grid-Connected Microgrids
hits.text: As the global energy transition accelerates, distribution systems are integrating increasing shares of inverter-interfaced renewables, making reliable voltage support a key operational requirement. In grid-connected microgrids, especially weak radial feeders in rural and remote areas, voltage-reactive power (Volt/Var) control must coordinate multiple inverters under uncertainty from photovoltaic (PV) intermittency, load volatility, and point-of-common-coupling (PCC) disturbances. Existing droop, model-based optimization, and non-graph reinforcement learning (RL) approaches often rely on fixed rules or do not explicitly exploit electrical topology, which limits adaptive coordination.
